sentences.text: 2 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:31963  CRL.P No. 8491 of 2021  ORAL ORDER 1.
This petition is filed by the husband and his relatives challenging the proceedings initiated by respondent No.2 for offences under Section 498A r/w Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. Today, a joint affidavit is filed in which the husband and wife have stated that they have settled the matter amicably and the husband is paying a sum of Rs.25 Lakhs in full and final settlement of his wife's claim.
It is also stated that a sum of Rs.23 Lakhs has been paid and it has been further undertaken that the balance of Rs.2 Lakhs would be paid at the time of signing the mediation agreement.

3. The terms of the joint affidavit read as follows:
"We, Mr.Piyush Rathod S/o Jinendra Kumar Jain, Aged about 32 years, Mr.Jinendra Kumar Jain S/o Bhabuthmal jain, aged about 56 years, Vidya Jain W/o Jinendra Kumar Jain, aged about 56 years, Esha Jain D/o Jinendra Kumar Jain, aged about 29 years, NC: 2024:KHC:31963 all of the above R/a # 379/7 Rajeshwari Nivas SB Road V V Puram, Bengaluru-560004 and Pooja Jain W/o Piyush Rathod Aged about 30 years, R/a 163 1st Main Road, Sheshadripuram, Bengaluru- 560020, do hereby solemnly state and affirm on oath as under:
1.That, we are the 2nd Respondent and Petitioners, OTAK respectively in the above matter and as such we are well conversant with the facts of the case.
Hence, we are competent to swear to the contents of this Affidavit.

2. That, the Petitioners and the 2nd Respondent have arrived at an amicable settlement wherein the 1st Petitioner has agreed to pay sum of Rs.25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Only) to the 2nd Respondent as full and final settlement (inclusive of permanent alimony) wherein a sum of Rs.21,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Only) is being paid by way of a Demand Draft bearing No.752464 dated 08.08.2024 drawn on State Bank of India, V.V.Puram Branch, Bengaluru in favour of the 2nd Respondent.

The remaining payment of Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs only)
is being paid by cash.
Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs) in cash is handed over along with the above mentioned Demand Draft to the 2nd Respondent on this day.

The 1 Petitioner undertakes to hand over the balance of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) in cash to NC: 2024:KHC:31963 the RespondentNo.2 at the time of signing mediation agreement In MC No.5438/2021.

2. That, the Petitioners and the 2nd Respondent have arrived at an amicable settlement wherein the 1st Petitioner has agreed to pay sum of Rs.25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakhs Only) to the 2nd Respondent as full and final settlement (inclusive of permanent alimony) wherein a sum of Rs.21,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty One Lakhs Only) is being paid by way of a Demand Draft bearing No.752464 dated 08.08.2024 drawn on State Bank of India, V.V.Puram Branch, Bengaluru in favour of the 2nd Respondent.
The remaining payment of Rs.4,00,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs only)
is being paid by cash.
Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs) in cash is handed over along with the above mentioned Demand Draft to the 2nd Respondent on this day.
The 1 Petitioner undertakes to hand over the balance of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) in cash to NC: 2024:KHC:31963 the RespondentNo.2 at the time of signing mediation agreement In MC No.5438/2021.
3. marriage of the 1 Petitioner and the 2nd Respondent shall be dissolved in MC No.5438/2021 pending adjudication before the 2nd Additional Family Judge at Bengaluru by getting the matter referred to mediation and thereafter, a settlement agreement would be drawn upon by the mediator and thereafter, the same shall attain finality by a Decree of Divorce that would be passed by the 2nd Additional Family Judge at Bengaluru in MC No.5438/2021.
4.
In view of the afore mentioned settlement agreed upon by the parties to the lis, the 2nd Respondent agrees and undertakes to withdraw the cases mentioned below for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court:
a) Cri.Misc No.41/2021 pending adjudication before the Judicial Magistrate First Class (Traffic Court-4) at Bengaluru;
b) Cri.Misc No.67/2023 pending adjudication before the Judicial Magistrate First Class (Traffic Court-4) at Bengaluru;
c) Cri. Misc No.116/2023 pending adjudication before the 2nd Additional Family Judge at Bengaluru;
NC: 2024:KHC:31963 5.
The 1st Petitioner undertakes to withdraw the case mentioned below for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court:
a) Criminal Appeal No.1131/2023 pending adjudication before the District and Sessions Judge (CCH-69) at Bengaluru 6.
7. That, as per the afore mentioned settlement, the 2 Respondent has agreed to consent by way of this joint affidavit for quashing of the Criminal Proceedings in CC No.17245/2020 pending adjudication before the 1 Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bengaluru for the offences punishable 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
registered by the 1st Respondent against the Petitioners.
8. That, the 2nd Respondent's claims have been settled in its entirety that she shall not have any claims in whatsoever nature as against the Petitioners and their immovable properties, The Petitioners shell not have any claims against the 2nd respondent and her family members.
That, the 2nd Respondent and Petitioners shall not defame each other in any public forum including social media and other platforms.
Hence, It is respectfully prayed that this Affidavit may be taken on record and this Hon'ble Court be pleased to quash the proceedings in the Criminal Proceedings in CC No.17245/2020 pending adjudication before the 1s Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bengaluru for the offences punishable 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 nod Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act registered toe 1st Respondent against the Petitioners and pass such other order/s as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit, proper, necessary and expedient in the circumstance of the case."
4.
In my view, having regard to the fact that the dispute between the parties was essentially private in nature and they have settled their differences amicably, no useful purpose would be served by continuing the proceedings.
In that view of the matter, the impugned proceedings pending in C.C.No.17245/2020 before the NC: 2024:KHC:31963 I Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate at Bangalore shall stand quashed.
